head_commit.message:
Support Command/Super shortcuts in the TUI keymap (#53754)

## What changed

- Accept `super` modifiers and normalize `cmd` and `command` aliases to `super`. Support capturing, displaying, and using these bindings in shortcuts, chords, and leaders.
- Add `super-left`, `super-right`, and `super-backspace` editor defaults for moving to the start or end of a line and deleting to its start.
- Honor safe Super-modified editor shortcuts during startup without treating them as text or inserting a pending paste newline.
- Save keymap edits through `config/value/write` when connected to a local daemon so it can validate bindings before they are saved or applied. Preserve the configuration and active keymap if the daemon rejects the edit.

## Testing

Add coverage for modifier aliases, shortcut capture and labels, chords and leaders, line editing, startup input, and daemon acceptance or rejection of keymap edits. Extend the startup PTY test with Command editing sequences.

head_commit.message:
Support Command/Super shortcuts in the TUI keymap (#53754)

## What changed

- Accept `super` modifiers and normalize `cmd` and `command` aliases to `super`. Support capturing, displaying, and using these bindings in shortcuts, chords, and leaders.
- Add `super-left`, `super-right`, and `super-backspace` editor defaults for moving to the start or end of a line and deleting to its start.
- Honor safe Super-modified editor shortcuts during startup without treating them as text or inserting a pending paste newline.
- Save keymap edits through `config/value/write` when connected to a local daemon so it can validate bindings before they are saved or applied. Preserve the configuration and active keymap if the daemon rejects the edit.

## Testing

Add coverage for modifier aliases, shortcut capture and labels, chords and leaders, line editing, startup input, and daemon acceptance or rejection of keymap edits. Extend the startup PTY test with Command editing sequences.

head_commit.message:
Extend copy-on-select to composer text (#53753)

## What changed

Apply `tui.copy_on_select` to composer mouse selections on release, including X11 PRIMARY publication when enabled. Keep editable selections highlighted so typing can replace the selected text, even when `tui.copy_on_select_clear_selection` is enabled.

Share clipboard destination handling across the transcript, footer, and composer. Apply automatic deselection to footer selections after confirmed delivery, and release composer and footer PRIMARY ownership on focus loss or resume. Update configuration descriptions to clarify the behavior across all three surfaces.

## Testing

Add composer tests covering copy on release, retained selection highlights, replacement by typing, PRIMARY ownership lifetime, and clipboard-only status reporting for pending copies.

head_commit.message:
Apply feature overrides when restarting the app-server daemon (#53751)

## Why

`codex app-server daemon restart` previously reused saved settings without applying feature flags supplied on the command line.

## What changed

Apply `--enable`, `--disable`, and boolean `-c features.*` overrides during an explicit restart and persist them for subsequent restarts. Accept nested `enabled` values, normalize feature aliases, and replace conflicting saved aliases while preserving unrelated settings.

Reject invalid feature toggles before stopping the daemon or saving settings.

## Testing

Add integration coverage for overrides on stopped and running daemons, alias replacement, preservation of saved settings, restarts without flags, and rejection of non-toggle keys without interrupting the running daemon.

head_commit.message:
Prefer remote Visualize installs over the bundled plugin (#53747)

## What changed

When the remote global catalog is active, let a cached `visualize@openai-curated-remote` install supersede `visualize@openai-bundled`, matching the existing Sites behavior. A disabled remote install also suppresses the bundled plugin; a missing remote bundle preserves the bundled fallback.

## Testing

Extend the agent-turn compatibility tests to cover Visualize with enabled, disabled, and missing remote bundles, asserting which skills appear in the developer prompt.
